question: Is the R2 (b++RRLL) SL(3) trace-map fixed locus 0-dimensional (sealing valid) or positive-dimensional (sealing fails)?
identification: b++RRLL = phi_2^2 = R^2L^2 = [[5,2],[2,1]] = silver m=2 once-punctured-torus bundle (census m136)
locus: Fix(T_2^2) on the 8 B48 SL(3) trace coordinates
headline: R2's fixed locus Fix(T_2^2) is POSITIVE-DIMENSIONAL: Krull dim = 2, and it stays dim 2 after the entire self-dual (SL(2)-derived / Sym^2) sub-locus is removed -- so R2's finite 50-point sample can never seal; the R2 sealing FAILS as a method
discriminating_fact: b++RRLL is the bundle monodromy phi_2^2 = R^2L^2 = [[5,2],[2,1]] (silver m=2, census m136). Its SL(3) trace-map fixed locus Fix(T_2^2) in the 8 B48 coordinates has KRULL DIMENSION 2, not 0: (i) grevlex Groebner over Q + Kredel-Weispfenning maximal-independent-set gives 2 with witness ['x3', 'x8']; (ii) an independent generic-slice certificate at 2 seeds gives exactly 2 (nonempty through 2 generic hyperplanes, ideal = (1) at 3); (iii) constructively, 5/5 random rational fibers over the witness pair are nonempty -- an explicit 2-parameter continuum of fixed characters. Crucially the same holds OFF the sub-locus: saturating by each of x1-x4, x2-x5, x3-x8, x6-x7 (which together cut out the self-dual locus, containing every SL(2)-derived family, i.e. B71's Sym^2 component V0 and any metallic sub-locus) leaves dimension {'x1 - x4': 2, 'x2 - x5': 2, 'x3 - x8': 2, 'x6 - x7': 2} with 5/5 nonempty generic fibers. m=1 calibration reproduces B71's figure-eight dim 2. This also reconciles B565/R2's own numeric 'local dim 10': 10 = 2 (character) + 8 (dim PGL(3,C) gauge orbit). A finite 50-point sample cannot seal a property over a 2-dimensional family.
terminal_state: CLOSED: the R2 sealing method is refuted -- the residual K-membership question needs a whole-family (2-parameter) argument, not point sampling
